propositions.text: The RPD received an application to reopen the Applicant's refugee claim on December 13, 2019.
propositions.quote: On December 13, 2019, the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB or the Board) received an application to reopen the refugee claim of XXXX XXXX XXXX (the Applicant)

propositions.text: The Applicant is a citizen of Democratic Republic of Congo.
propositions.quote: a citizen of Democratic Republic of Congo

propositions.text: The earlier RPD decision on October 31, 2019 concluded the claim had been abandoned.
propositions.quote: following an RPD decision made on October 31, 2019, concluding that the claim had been abandoned.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RPD received the Applicant's reopening application on December 13, 2019, after an October 31, 2019 abandonment decision.

propositions.text: The RPD's jurisdiction to reopen a claim is limited and only exercisable if a breach of natural justice is established.
propositions.quote: The RPD's jurisdiction to reopen a claim is limited since once the decision is made, the RPD becomes functus officio and could exercise its jurisdiction again only if a breach to a principle of natural justice is established.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the RPD can only reopen claims if a natural justice breach is shown.

propositions.text: The Applicant's claim was referred to the IRB on October 4, 2019.
propositions.quote: On October 4, 2019, the claim of the Applicant was referred to the IRB.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the claim was referred to the IRB on October 4, 2019.

propositions.text: On October 4, 2019, the Applicant was advised to provide the Basis of Claim Form within 15 days or face a special hearing on October 28, 2019.
propositions.quote: On the same date, the Applicant was given a document entitled Confirmation of referral and Notice to Appear at the RPD, in which the Applicant was advised that she had 15 days to provide the Basis of Claim Form (BOC) and that, should she fail to provide the BOC within the 15-day deadline, a special hearing would be held on October 28, 2019

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Applicant was given 15 days to submit the BOC or face a special hearing on October 28, 2019.

propositions.text: A special hearing was held on October 28, 2019, which the Applicant did not attend.
propositions.quote: A special hearing was held on October 28, 2019, at which the Applicant did not appear.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Applicant did not appear at the October 28, 2019 special hearing.

propositions.text: Counsel of record since October 13, 2019, also did not appear at the special hearing.
propositions.quote: Although counsel is counsel of record since October 13, 2019, he too, did not appear on that date.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found counsel also failed to appear at the special hearing.

propositions.text: Due to the Applicant's default, the claim was pronounced abandoned on October 28, 2019.
propositions.quote: As a consequence of the Applicant's default to appear, the abandonment of her claim was pronounced on the same date, October 28,2019.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the claim was abandoned on October 28, 2019 due to Applicant's default.

propositions.text: On October 30, 2019, the RPD sent the Notice of Decision - Abandonment to the Applicant's address of record.
propositions.quote: On October 30, 2019, the RPD forwarded to the Applicant, at the address of record, a Notice of Decision - Abandonment of a claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Notice of Abandonment was sent to the Applicant on October 30, 2019.

propositions.text: On November 4, 2019, the Applicant notified the Board of a new address.
propositions.quote: On November 4, 2019, the Applicant forwarded to the Board a Notification of Client Contact Information in which she advised the Board of her new address.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Applicant notified the Board of a new address on November 4, 2019.

propositions.text: On November 25, 2019, the Notice of Decision was returned by the Post Office marked 'Moved/Unknown'.
propositions.quote: On November 25, 2019, the Board's letter containing the Notice of Decision - Abandonment of a claim for refugee protection was returned by the Post Office with the note "Moved/Uknown".

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Notice was returned undelivered on November 25, 2019.

propositions.text: The Board sent the Notice of Decision to the new address on November 27, 2019.
propositions.quote: The Board forwarded the Notice of Decision to the new address of record on November 27, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Notice was forwarded to the new address on November 27, 2019.

propositions.text: The Board received the application to reopen the claim on December 13, 2019.
propositions.quote: As stated above, the Board received an application to reopen the claim of the Applicant on December 13, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Board received the reopening application on December 13, 2019.

propositions.text: Counsel states the BOC was submitted within the expected timeframe on October 13, 2019, supported by a fax copy.
propositions.quote: In this application, counsel for the Applicant states that the BOC was "submitted with the timeframe it was expected to be file (sic) (2019-10-13) as appears on a copy of the fax attached".

paragraphs.summary: The applicant's counsel argues the BOC was submitted on time on October 13, 2019, supported by a fax copy.

propositions.text: The fax receipt attached is dated December 12, 2019, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada, indicating 26 pages.
propositions.quote: The attachment to which counsel is referring is a Fax receipt dated December 12, 2019 at 20:49, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada stating "Veuillez trouver ci-joint une correspondance à porter à votre attention ", indicating that there are 26 pages.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the fax receipt attached is dated December 12, 2019, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada.

propositions.text: The attachment contains BOCs signed October 13, 2019 but date-stamped by the Board on December 13, 2019.
propositions.quote: The attachment also contains the BOCs of the Applicant and the minor child which would have been signed on October 13, 2019 but which bears a date stamp from the Board, two months later, that is, on December 13, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the BOCs were signed October 13, 2019 but date-stamped by the Board on December 13, 2019.

propositions.text: The Board processed the BOCs in its system on December 19, 2019.
propositions.quote: The Board processed the BOCs in its case management system, NOVA, on December 19, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Board processed the BOCs on December 19, 2019.

propositions.text: It is unknown why counsel claims the BOCs were received on October 13, 2019 as no evidence supports this.
propositions.quote: It is not known why counsel states in his application that the BOCs would have been received by the Board on October 13, 2019 as there is no evidence of this fact, whether in the attachment provided by counsel or in the Board's record.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence supports counsel's claim that the BOCs were received on October 13, 2019.

propositions.text: While BOCs may have been signed October 13, 2019, they were provided to the Board only on December 13, 2019.
propositions.quote: While the BOCs may have been signed on October 13, 2019, they were provided to the Board 2 months later, on December 13, 2019 as appears from the Board's date stamp.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the BOCs were signed October 13, 2019 but provided to the Board on December 13, 2019.

propositions.text: The fax shows BOCs may have been sent to Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada on December 12, 2019 but not to the Board.
propositions.quote: The fax attachment to counsel's Application to reopen shows that the BOCs may have been forwarded to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada, on December 12, 2019 but it does not show that it was provided to the Board.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the fax shows BOCs sent to Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada but not to the Board.

propositions.text: The fax receipt is dated December 12, 2020 but the BOCs are stamped December 13, 2020, so they could not have been attached to the fax.
propositions.quote: Moreover, while the Fax's receipt is dated December 12, 2020, the attachment (the BOCs) are stamped December 13, 2020, one day after the fax was sent, which means that they could not have been attached to the Fax receipt.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the fax receipt and BOC dates conflict, indicating the BOCs were not attached to the fax.

propositions.text: The tribunal asked the Applicant to provide proof that the application to reopen was forwarded to the Minister per RPD Rule 62(2).
propositions.quote: The tribunal then asked the Applicant to provide proof that the application to reopen this file be forwarded to the Minister in accordance with RPD Rule 62 (2).

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal asked the Applicant to prove forwarding the reopening application to the Minister as required by RPD Rule 62(2).

propositions.text: On January 23, 2020, the Applicant provided a fax receipt dated December 12, 2019, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada, indicating 26 pages.
propositions.quote: On January 23, 2020, the Applicant provided the same document to which it is referred in paragraph 14 of the present decision, namely a Fax receipt dated December 12, 2019 at 20:49, addressed to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada stating "Veuillez trouver ci-joint une correspondance à porter à votre attention ", indicating that there are 26 pages.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant provided a December 12, 2019 fax receipt to the Ministère de la sécurité publique du Canada showing 26 pages were sent.

propositions.text: The tribunal concludes the Applicant did not comply with Rule 62(2) and this may be seen as an attempt to mislead the Tribunal.
propositions.quote: The tribunal concludes that the Applicant did not comply with Rule 62 (2) and this action on his part could be interpreted as an attempt to mislead the Tribunal.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds the Applicant failed to comply with Rule 62(2) and may have tried to mislead the Tribunal.

propositions.text: The tribunal finds no breach of natural justice principles has been established in this case.
propositions.quote: The tribunal finds that, in the circumstances of this case, a breach to a principle of natural justice has not been established.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal finds no breach of natural justice principles was established here.

propositions.text: The tribunal denies the Applicant's application to reopen the claim after considering all circumstances.
propositions.quote: After having considered the application of the Applicant and the circumstances as a whole, the tribunal determines that the Application to reopen the claim of the Applicant is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The tribunal denies the Applicant's application to reopen the claim after full consideration.
